Md. Maqbul Ahmed, Advocate, instructed by A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record. ----- For the Petitioners.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 3.8.2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4479 of 1995).
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J : This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 3.8.2005 passed a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4479 of 1995 making absolute the Rule obtained against the judgment and order dated 19.8.1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd court, Chittagong, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 219 of 1991 reversing those of dated 20.8.1991 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Raozan, Chittagong, in Miscellaneous Case No. 24 of 1988 allowing pre-emption.

<u>2. The respondent No. 1 instituted the above miscellaneous case for pre-emption of the case land measuring 9½ decimals of land under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act or in the alternative under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act 1949, on the averments that the above land originally belonged to Yunus Mia Chowdhury, the opposite party No.2, who sold the same to Amina Khatoon, the predecessor of the opposite party No.1 by registered sale deed dated 27.7.87 which was entered in the volume on 23.2.88; Amina Khatoon is a stranger to the case jote; the notice of the above sale deed being collusively suppressed, the pre-emptor, a co-sharer of the case jote, had no knowledge of the above transfer and he came to know about the same only on 3.4.88 and thereafter on 11.4.1988 he filed this miscellaneous case.</u>

3. The pre-emptee petitioner contested the case by filing written objection denying all the material allegations and contending that the pre-emptor not being a co-sharer the case for pre-emption is liable to be rejected.

4. The learned Assistant Judge, after hearing, allowed the pre-emption holding that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer. On appeal the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court Chittagong, after hearing, allowed the appeal holding that the pre-emptor is' not co-sharer. The respondent No.1 then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 4479 of 1994 and after hearing, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that B.S. Record, Ext.3, and the sale deed Ext. 5 (Ka) by which the pre-emptor purchased his land in the case jote, clearly show that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the case jote and the finding of the appellate Court to the effect that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer in the case jote being not based on correct assessment of the evidence on record can not be sustained.

5. The learned counsel for the pre-emptee petitioner submits that the High Court Division fell in error in not considering that the deed dated 27.7.87, against which pre-emption is sought, is not in fact a transfer deed as in the same value of the case land was shown at merely Tk. 98/- and further the possession of the land covered under the above deed was also not delivered and so the above deed may be termed as a deed for protection of possession of the pre-emptee petitioner against which a pre-emption case is not maintainbale; the appellate Court correctly found that the pre-emptee is not wholly a stranger in view of the fact that her husband Ranju Miah was one of the co-sharers in the R.S. Khatian No. 2480 and further as the B.S. Record was not correctly prepared and for that the recorded tenant executed and registered the above deed dated 27.7.87 for removal of that mistake and the said deed as is in fact not a sale deed; the High Court Division having had failed to take notice that the pre-emptee petitioner was not a stranger to the case jote and that she has been possessing the case land and residing in the homestead situated therein for long time and if the pre-emption case is allowed the paternal homestead of the petitioner will go into the hand of the pre-emptor.

<u>6. As it appears the High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that the pre-emptor purchased a portion of the case jote by Ext. 5(Ka) and his name was recorded in the B.S. record, Ext.3, in Khatian No. 54 and the rent receipts Ext.4 series, also show that he, after purchasing the said land, mutated his name and paid rents regularly and he, as co-sharer, is in possession in the case land and the B.S. Khatian which has been published finally does not contain the name of the pre-emptee and the pre-emptee has also not challenged that preparation of B.S. Khatian in the name of the pre-emptor and so prima facie the pre-emptor appears to be a co-sharer and further the title of the pre-emptor in the case land can be challenged by the pre-emptee only in a properly constituted title suit.</u>

7. We are of the view that the High Court Division on proper consideration of the evidence and the materials on record arrived at a correct decision. The learned counsel could not point at any illegality or infirmity in the decision of the High Court Division so as to call for any interference.

8. The petition is dismissed.

End.
